selected_problem: Fresh main bound non-force push to the expected validated commit, but GitHub pull-request merge still treated expectedHeadSha as optional. A PR head could therefore move after review/validation and an unbound merge request would accept GitHub's then-current head instead of the validated candidate.

decision_provenance.mode_route_basis: One narrow evidence-rich remote-delivery artifact-binding gap remained after exact-object push binding, so the committed singular-bottleneck gate routes the replay to DEEP_DEVELOPMENT without forced mode rotation.
decision_provenance.claim_limit: No hosted DWAC success receipt or fabricated numeric score is claimed.

pre_fix_reproduction.source_observation: githubMergePullRequest only added GitHub REST `sha` when expectedHeadSha happened to be supplied; otherwise it issued a merge request with only merge_method.
pre_fix_reproduction.consequence: The provider had no fail-closed guarantee that the PR head being merged was the exact previously validated candidate.

changes: githubMergePullRequest now requires a concrete expectedHeadSha before making any GitHub merge API call.
Missing or malformed expected heads fail closed with EXPECTED_HEAD_SHA_REQUIRED or EXPECTED_HEAD_SHA_INVALID and perform no merge side effect.
Every accepted merge request always sends the expected head as the GitHub REST merge `sha` precondition.
gitRemoteDelivery propagates the merge hard-gate error instead of collapsing it into a generic PR_MERGE_FAILED result.

cases: missing and malformed expected heads return before the mocked GitHub API is invoked
valid expected head is present verbatim as the merge request body sha precondition
validation.unchanged_regression_basis: The push and PR-creation paths were unchanged from v0.10.7, where the focused remote-provider harness passed 3/3 against real local/bare Git plus mocked GitHub REST.

truth_boundaries: This makes expected PR head identity mandatory at the provider merge boundary; it does not independently prove review/check state, which remains subject to repository rules and caller policy.
GitHub itself enforces the supplied head SHA precondition; if the PR head moved, the merge must fail rather than silently adopt the new head.
No force push, repository-rule bypass, credential exposure, payment, formal Release, or destructive/irreversible external action is introduced.
OS-level validation sandboxing, arbitrary complex semantic synthesis, Windows descendant-tree equivalence, and crash-level filesystem atomicity remain unresolved.
